text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- General Workers' Union members approve new dockyard measures, including direct government representation on Drydocks managing council.

- Government-appointed task force approves measures to modernise Malta Drydocks, recommending changes to management, tighter financial control, and recruitment of training managers and consultants, including foreigners.
- Teacher shortage hitting all sectors of education, with primary school suffering most.
- Dockyard workers, in meeting with Prime Minister Alfred Sant, blame managers for dockyard's ills.
- Prime minister calls for consensus on Malta Drydocks issue.

- Opposition complains at government "arrogance" over Drydocks legislation. The opposition has been angered by government plans to move amendments to the Malta Drydocks law in parliament next Saturday, only four days after publication of the draft law changing the composition of the Malta Drydocks Council. The opposition said more time should have been given for it to study the proposals.
